tips: Master the Pencil Button - Toggle pencil mode with the ✏️ button. When lit, you mark candidates; when dark, you place digits. Press P on keyboard for quick toggle.
Long-Press the Pencil for All Candidates - Hold the pencil button to reveal all valid candidates instantly across every empty cell. Let the website show you the possibilities.
Long-Press Numbers for Candidates - Hold any number button (not just tap) to mark it as a candidate. Tap places the digit, long-press marks potential.
The Hint Button is Your Teacher - When stuck, click Hint. A confirmation appears with wisdom, then reveals the best strategic move highlighted in green. Study why that cell was chosen.
Click Strategies to See Your Path - The Strategies link shows which solving techniques apply to your current puzzle. Each puzzle tells you what methods it requires.
Mark All Errors to Check Progress - Click Mark All Errors for a one-time reveal of incorrect cells outlined in red. Any board action clears the highlighting. Use wisely—learning beats checking.

Enable Auto-Clean for Automatic Help - Toggle the auto-clean switch under the controls. After 5 seconds, placed digits remove themselves from peer candidates automatically, with yellow borders showing cleaned cells.
Yellow Borders Show Auto-Cleaned Cells - When auto-clean activates, affected cells glow with golden borders for 5 seconds, showing where pencil marks were removed.
Undo Remembers Everything - Press Ctrl+Z or tap Undo (↶) to step backward through your moves. Auto-clean is fully undoable: first undo restores candidates, second removes the digit.
The Timer Starts with First Move - TOTAL FUN TIME begins when you touch the board or keypad. It auto-pauses after 60 seconds of inactivity or window blur (with 5-second grace period).
Pause is Rest, Not Failure - When the pause modal appears, click Resume when ready. The timer waits patiently; mastery requires breaks.
Reset Clears Everything with Confirmation - The Reset link opens a confirmation modal. Accepting wipes all progress, candidates, and history. The path begins anew.

Share Your Victory on Facebook - The Share button copies your completion post (puzzle number, difficulty, time, and solved grid) to clipboard, then opens Facebook's share dialog. Paste and inspire others.
Print Puzzles for Offline Practice - Click Print in the header. Choose normal or large format. The grid prints cleanly without timer or highlights.
View the Puzzle Quote - Some puzzles display an italic quote beneath the header. Samurai wisdom accompanies your practice.
Each Puzzle Has Its Own Number - The header shows "Sudoku #X - DIFFICULTY". Share this number with friends so they can solve the same puzzle.
Help Contains Full Instructions - Click Help in the header for complete rules, controls, keyboard shortcuts, and contact email (openmindbooks1@gmail.com).
Free Sample Link in Header - Get a taste of the Samurai Sudoku book before purchasing. The link opens a pre-download confirmation modal.
Keyboard is Faster Than Mouse - Arrow keys navigate. Numbers 1-9 place digits. Backspace/Delete/Space clear cells. Tab moves forward. Master the keyboard path.
On-Screen Keypad Layout - Two rows, six buttons each. Row 1: digits 1-5 plus Pencil. Row 2: digits 6-9 plus Clear and Undo. Uniform and always visible.
Touch and Mouse Both Work - The site responds to mouse clicks, keyboard input, and touch gestures. Choose the tool that fits your hand.
Clear Button Empties Cells - The ⌫ button removes the current cell's value. History remembers; undo can restore it.
Blue Numbers Are Immutable Givens - The puzzle's foundation appears in blue. You cannot change these; they anchor the truth.
Your Numbers Appear in Black - Digits you enter show in black. Distinguish your work from the given clues at a glance.
Red Means Conflict - Duplicate numbers in any row, column, or box turn red instantly. Resolve conflicts before continuing.
Active Cell Shows Border and Background - The selected cell has a 2px outline and 12% background. When you select a filled cell, all cells with that same number highlight identically.
Empty Cell Selection Shows No Highlights - Select a blank cell and no other cells glow. The empty seeks its destiny alone.
Bold Lines Separate 3×3 Boxes - Thick borders define the nine boxes. Use these visual boundaries to scan effectively.
Green Highlight Marks Hints - Hinted cells glow green until your next action. This visual cue teaches strategic thinking.
Pencil Marks Use Fixed 3×3 Layout - Candidates appear in mini-grids matching digit positions 1-9. This consistency builds visual pattern memory.
Progress Saves Automatically - Your work is preserved for one hour. Return and continue exactly where you left off.
Progress Clears on Completion - When you solve a puzzle, saved progress is erased. Victory brings a fresh start.
The Empty Mind Wins - Clear your thoughts before you begin. A calm mind sees patterns the rushing eye cannot perceive.
Start with the Obvious - As the samurai strikes the exposed flank first, fill the naked singles before seeking hidden truths.
Scan the Horizon - Survey the entire grid before committing. The whole battlefield reveals opportunities the single cell conceals.
Count Your Forces - In each row, column, and box, count what remains unfilled. The smallest gaps yield the quickest victories.
The Box is Your Dojo - Master the 3×3 boxes first. A strong foundation in small spaces builds strength across the field.
Row and Column Unite - Where row meets column in a box, the intersection reveals destiny. Seek these crossing points.
One Number, One Journey - Follow a single digit across the grid. Where can 5 live? The path becomes clear when you seek but one.
The Last Stand - When eight warriors occupy a row, the ninth has no choice. Seek these final positions for swift progress.
Hidden Singles Await - Like a ninja in shadow, some numbers hide in plain sight—the only candidate in their domain.
Naked Pairs Stand Together - Two cells with identical two candidates? No other cell in their domain may hold those numbers.
Hidden Pairs Lurk Beneath - Two candidates appear only in two cells within a group? Those cells belong to those numbers alone.
X-Wing Soars Above - When a candidate forms corners of a rectangle across rows and columns, eliminate it from crossing lines.
Swordfish Cuts Deep - The advanced warrior sees three rows and three columns forming a pattern. Master this, and hard puzzles yield.
Box-Line Reduction - If a candidate appears only in one row within a box, eliminate it from that row outside the box.
Pointing Pairs Reveal Truth - When two cells in a box share a candidate aligned in one row/column, clear it from the rest of that line.
Pencil Marks Are Your Map - The careful warrior marks possibilities before choosing. Small green numbers light your path.
Toggle with Intent - The pencil button is your tool. When lit, you mark possibilities; when dark, you claim certainty.
Start with Full Candidates - In difficult puzzles, mark all possibilities first. The forest reveals the path when all trees are visible.
Candidates Narrow the Way - With pencil marks, count candidates per cell. Cells with fewest options demand attention first.
Auto-Clean Aids Your Path - Enable the auto-clean toggle. When a digit remains unchanged for five seconds, it removes itself from peer candidates automatically.
Yellow Borders Guide You - Auto-cleaned cells glow with golden borders for five seconds. These marks show where logic has swept away impossibility.
Clean as You Go - When you place a digit, remove it from peers. The auto-clean feature aids this discipline.
Click Strategies for Guidance - The Strategies link shows which techniques apply to your current puzzle. Let the puzzle's own wisdom guide you.
The Hint Button Offers Insight - When blocked, click Hint. The path to mastery is built on moments of insight—receive one, and grow stronger.
Green Highlights Point the Way - Hinted cells glow green until your next move. Study why this cell was chosen.
Undo is Not Retreat - Press Ctrl+Z or tap Undo to step backward. Even the greatest swordsman adjusts their stance.
Clear Removes, Not Erases History - The Clear button empties a cell. Use it freely; undo remembers your past.
Mark All Errors Once - Click Mark All Errors to reveal incorrect entries in red outline. Use sparingly—learn from mistakes rather than depend on checking.
No Errors Means Victory Approaches - When "No errors found—you are going great!" appears, your path is true. Persist.
Reset Requires Confirmation - The Reset link clears all progress. A modal asks for certainty—this action is irreversible.
The Timer Measures Joy, Not Pressure - TOTAL FUN TIME counts your engagement, not your stress. Speed follows mastery, not the reverse.
Pause Means Rest, Not Defeat - After 60 seconds of inactivity or window blur, the timer pauses. Even the sharpest blade must rest in its sheath.
Share Your Victory - When complete, the Share button copies your triumph to clipboard. Paste into Facebook and inspire others.
Print for Practice - Click Print in the header to print puzzles. Choose normal or large format. Practice on paper sharpens the digital mind.
Help is Always Available - Click Help in the header for detailed controls, rules, and contact information. openmindbooks1@gmail.com
Get the Free Sample - The Free Sample link in the header offers a taste of the Samurai Sudoku book before you commit.
Quote Inspires the Mind - Some puzzles show an italic quote beneath the header. Let wisdom accompany your journey.
Each Puzzle Has a Number - Share specific puzzles with friends using the puzzle number in the header. Guide others to the same challenge.
Keyboard Controls Master - Arrow keys navigate cells. Numbers 1-9 place digits. Backspace, Delete, or Space clear cells. Tab moves forward. Simple tools for complex battles.
On-Screen Keypad Always Ready - Two rows, six buttons each. Top row: 1-5 and Pencil. Bottom row: 6-9, Clear, and Undo. Uniform layout for swift action.
Touch and Click Both Work - The website responds to mouse, keyboard, and touch. Choose your weapon.
P Toggles Pencil Mode - Press P on keyboard to quickly switch between placing digits and marking candidates.
Blue Numbers Are Given - The puzzle's foundation appears in blue. These are your anchors—immutable truth.
Black Numbers Are Yours - Your entered digits appear in black. Distinguish your work from the given path.
Red Means Conflict - Duplicate numbers in a row, column, or box turn red instantly. Correct this before proceeding.
Active Cell Has a Border - The selected cell shows a border with background. Focus follows your attention.
Same Numbers Highlight Together - Select a filled cell, and all cells with that number glow identically. See patterns across the grid.
Empty Selection Shows No Highlight - When you select an empty cell, no other cells highlight. The blank seeks its identity alone.
Bold Lines Define Boxes - 3×3 boxes have thick borders. Let these boundaries guide your scanning.
Strategies Vary by Difficulty - Easy puzzles need naked singles; hard puzzles demand advanced patterns. Read the strategies list to know your enemy.
Every Puzzle Has a Solution - Completion is always possible. The path exists; you need only find it.
The Path to Mastery Is Built on Practice - Each puzzle strengthens your pattern recognition. Play daily, and what seems impossible today becomes effortless tomorrow.

Progress Clears on Victory - When you complete a puzzle, saved progress is cleared. Begin fresh with the next challenge.
